maya: FYI prod canary for embeddings-service is throwing 502s from the edge LB, rolling it back for now. health check = unhealthy. anyone seeing this in us-west2?
ash: seeing same. ALB target group shows failed health checks, connection timed out. no recent deploys AFAIK.
liam: I ssh'd into a bastion and tried curl to the nodeport via the LB public ip — connection refused/timeout. From inside the VPC to the node ip it works.
devops-jordan: quick check: public subnet NACLs were touched last week for a lockdown sweep. lemme pull the rules.
devops-jordan: (running) `aws ec2 describe-network-acls --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=subnet-0abc123`
devops-jordan: output shows a DENY for TCP ports 32768-65535 with rule #100 and an ALLOW for 0-1024 with rule #50.
sre-ashley: ah — NACLs are stateless and evaluated by rule number; that DENY will block ephemeral source ports used by the ALB health checks (health checks originate from LB using ephemeral source ports). That explains public->node connectivity failing while intra-VPC works.
maya: oh nice catch. so ALB health checks hit nodeport with source port in ephemeral range, NACL denies inbound, target marked unhealthy.
liam: can confirm: traceroute from outside shows RST/timeout at subnet boundary.
devops-jordan: plan: add ALLOW rule for TCP 32768-61000 with priority 55 (between 50 and 100) for both inbound/outbound on the public subnet NACLs, then test canary.
devops-jordan: applying with CLI:```bash
# inbound
aws ec2 create-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0f12abcd --rule-number 55 --protocol tcp --port-range From=32768,To=61000 --egress false --rule-action allow
# outbound
aws ec2 create-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0f12abcd --rule-number 55 --protocol tcp --port-range From=32768,To=61000 --egress true --rule-action allow
```
opsbot: Created incident INC-2345: "ALB health checks failing due to NACL ephemeral port deny" assigned to devops-jordan. :rotating_light:
devops-jordan: added rules, propagation ~30s. re-registering targets now.
sre-ashley: note for postmortem: avoid implicit DENY rules that block ephemeral ranges. prefer explicit allow list first or use security groups for stateful control. we'll add a linter for infra PRs that touches NACLs.
maya: retesting canary — sending traffic to embeddings-service v2 canary.
maya: canary succeeded, health checks green, no 502s observed. :tada:
liam: double-checking metrics — latency stable and no errors.
ash: great. moving to close the rollback.
maya: thanks team. adding a short runbook note under infra/networking for ephemeral port gotchas.
opsbot: Incident INC-2345 updated: resolved by devops-jordan.
maya: closing thread. :white_check_mark:
